Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. Nitin Kamal, learned counsel
for the petitioner through V.C.
2. Mr. Suyash Pant, learned
Standing Counsel for the
State/respondent no. 1 to 3.
3. The petitioner has purchased a
vehicle from respondent no.4, dealer
of Hyundai Vehicle situated at
Haridwar by pass road Dehradun.
4. It is the contention of petitioner
that the said vehicle was not a brand
new one rather it was already
registered in the name of one Kaif
Malik. The petitioner alleged cheating
and deficiency in service by the
respondent no.4.
5. It is contended by learned

UKHC010186832026
2026:UHC:9547
counsel for petitioner that he has
already made an application under
Section 175(3) of BNSS, 2023 in the
Court of Judicial Magistrate Haridwar
and at the same time it is also
contended by the learned counsel for
the petitioner that a complaint is also
filed before the District Consumer
Forum.
6. From perusal of the record it
transpires that the petitioner has
allegedly been cheated and service
was deficient by the dealer, therefore
in such case the State authority has
no involvement at all, therefore, the
writ petition cannot be maintained in
the way its filed.
7. Accordingly, the writ petition is
dismissed.
 (Pankaj Purohit, J.)
 16.10.2026
